To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a large unlabeled food domain-specific corpus is a valuable resource that allows us to automatically assign semantic information to a food item; 2) the usage of a food domain-specific corpus outperforms a manually designed open domain ontology; 3) our categorizations outperform state-of-the-art syntactic features and Brown clustering.
the induction of a domain-specific ontology from a large corpus is useful for relation extraction.
